subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
cluster: Forces at a distance and materials
skillName: Structure of Materials and Their Properties

items.prompt:
A material's properties are explained by its
A) molecular structure and particle attractions
B) color only
C) price
D) name
items.answer: A) molecular structure and particle attractions

items.prompt:
Strong attractions between particles make a material
A) hard
B) soft
C) invisible
D) lighter

steps: Strong attractions make a material hard.

items.prompt:
A flexible molecular structure lets a material
A) bend without breaking
B) only shatter
C) never move
D) melt instantly

A material with strong particle attractions tends to have a ____ melting point.
A) high
B) low
C) zero
D) negative

steps: Strong attractions give a high melting point.

items.prompt:
Rubber is chosen for a tire because its structure is
A) flexible, letting it bend
B) brittle
C) very hard
D) heavy

A hard material is good for a
A) cutting tool
B) stretchy band
C) soft pillow
D) flexible hose

Understanding a material's molecular structure helps engineers
A) choose or design materials with the right properties for a job
B) ignore properties
C) set the price
D) name the material
items.answer: A) choose or design materials with the right properties for a job

steps: Structure guides material choice and design.

items.prompt:
Why does a strongly-bonded material have a high melting point?
A) More energy is needed to separate the tightly held particles
B) It has no particles
C) Weak bonds hold it
D) It is always cold
items.answer: A) More energy is needed to separate the tightly held particles

steps: Strong bonds need more energy to melt.
